title: A Beautiful Experience with Huge Potential
content:
I’m enjoying Portal a lot. It’s relaxing, immersive, and very useful while working, reading, or unwinding.

As someone who enjoys photography and uses a Nikon Z7 II, I also appreciate how difficult it would be to capture scenes like this myself. You would need the right location, timing, composition, high-resolution video, natural sound, stabilization, and careful editing. Portal brings that whole atmosphere instantly to the Mac.

That said, I think the next big step would be adding more depth and true 3D environments. After some time, it becomes clear that some scenes are repeated video loops. A more dynamic environment, with subtle 3D movement and non-repeating details, would make it feel much more alive.

I’d also love to see an iPad version. Many heavy Mac users — developers, designers, and professionals — also use iPads or MacBooks. Imagine Portal extending one continuous scene across multiple Apple screens, creating a panoramic workspace environment. That would be a fantastic use of the Apple ecosystem.

Overall, this is already an excellent app, and I’m excited to see where it goes next. Five stars.

title: Simply a Great App!
content:
I have the Portal app on all the time, rotating scenes automatically every hour. The scenery is beautiful and the sounds immersive and calming. I even have one desktop space set up with no apps in it so I can go there, hide my menu bar and dock with a single shortcut, and simply enjoy the sights and sounds – it becomes a window to nature.

I suppose one can put together screensavers with sounds or YouTube videos to produce a similar effect for one location. But I don't think it would be nearly as easy to manage all of the locations and switch from one to the other with the ease Portal provides. It has a beautiful interface with lots of options. And then there's the settings panel with even more customization available.

Given the subscription fee (or the one-time lifetime membership cost), I think this is one of the best additions to my Mac, and I recommend it to all of my friends. And if you have any questions, Portal’s support team is quick to respond and provides very personal and thorough assistance.

An enthusiastic thumbs-up for the app and the company!

title: Glad The Devs Woke Up
content:
I love this app and have been using it for years. I don’t think I’ve ever found any other app with comparable audio quality and ofc the visuals are second to none. Youtube does offer mixes of similar quality, but those are prepackaged and often repeated ad nauseum until you’re sick of the same ‘crashing waves asmr’ sound. These mixes help me sleep, help me work and help me feel better broadly. I’ve spent MANY a busy work shift with these playing in my ear and without it I’m sure I’d only be half as useful to my team lol. 

With all that said, only in the last month have I actually paid for a subscription. Previously the full app was like, 300 dollars for a lifetime account and the annual was 100-200 dollars or some other ludicrous number. Even the monthly was 50-90 dollars or something, and for all the love I had from this app I could never in good faith pay for that. I was tempted on multiple occasions to pay the whatever the hell and be done, but it actually felt sacrilegious to give 3 digits to a asmr machine when Youtube was (terrible) free. It seems the Dev team has come to see reason and changed their price with the new subscription price being 100 for a lifetime account and 30 for an annual subscription. If they’d caught me even a week earlier with my new paycheck sitting in my account, I’d have gotten the lifetime account. They didn’t so I only have the annual account for now (a safe choice, if I decide to suddenly stop using it almost 8 years in lol) but I love getting to listen to more then 4 mixes. It’s honestly been a bit overwhelming hahaha.

Anyway, I love the app! Only thing keeping me from giving a full 5 stars is just that the selection is a bit repetitive (each perfect, but repetitive) and I’d like a bit of variety in the sounds offered (underwater mix, crowd mix, farm mix, horses on a road etc etc). I hope the team can travel and take in more locations and countries, I’d personally request one that’s on the outskirts of a city or something, hearing the life of the people in whatever little European village but not actually drenched in noise. But, digressing. If you read all this, get the app.

title: MUST HAVE! Your window to nature and relaxation. Nothing else like it.
content:
I’m serious about the title. This is something everyone can benefit from installing and using. Outstanding quality video and audio!

I’ve looked for over a decade for long form video that is stationary with amazing quality and audio to match. Finally found it. Portal is worth every penny.

My need: A window. My office is windowless. 

Back in the day, my mother got a call from my second grade teacher because I wasn’t paying attention in class… I was staring out the window daydreaming all the time.

Now I’m lucky to have multiple monitors and I've often put window-swap(dot)com full screen in one monitor, but they don’t curate their videos (they’re user submitted) and there’s a lot of sub-par stuff. It is fun to see what others experience. 

At the same time, I’m very very picky and when I need to concentrate or relax, I don’t want to sift thru the trash to find the nuggets… Portal is now the only choice because they curate excellence.

Looking around the ‘net, you’ll find a ton of drone video of beautiful beaches or mountains, often with horrible music playing. That’s not for me.

I sent Chatgpt out to find my perfect window videos and it said it couldn’t find them. Everything it found was either garbage or an ad for a hotel. #useless.

My son-in-law just gave me a 4k TV for my office and it is now my ‘window’ with Portal running on it full time. I’m in daydreaming heaven. 

I wanted a window and now I have it!

Pros: beautiful app design. Amazing 4k+ videos with Spatial Audio on most. This team cares about high quality! 

Cons: (I've only had the app a week but feel compelled to tell the world!) I’ve told the team already, but (and I told you I was picky) some of the video with waves for example the sound doesn’t match the waves which causes a bit of disjointed experience for me. But that’s a nit. 

Summary:

This is exactly the app I’ve been lusting to have for at least a decade. Soothing, visually stunning, wide variety of 4,6, and even 8k video. So well thought out and so great getting back in touch with nature, even when you can’t leave the house. 

Incredibly versatile too… you can play in a window, make it full screen if you want, or you can have the app put the video on your desktop! Plus you can download the videos if you need to travel. 

So beautifully designed and deserves many awards.

Plus! I almost forgot… if you have smart home lights, you can connect and the app will match the room lighting to the mood. 

Oh, and the team is great with support. I’ve already sent in half a dozen suggestions because I'm just so excited about this!

title: Temper your expectations if you're not rich
content:
The app looks and sounds gorgeous. You get 6 soundscapes + their visuals for free. There's also a focus timer, alarm, and breathing exercises available (although the UI is confusing with the Focus / Sleep / Escape "modes"). 

But for the full experience, it feels like you have to be wealthy. The app itself is $5.83/mo or $300 for a lifetime license. There's no Android version, so if I ever wanted to change phones in the future I'd be out $300. 

That price doesn't sound worth it to me for 100 soundscapes alone, so to really make it worth it, I'd want to take advantage of the premium features. I'd need a nice screen for the visuals (like a 4K or better TV), a good set of earphones for the dynamic Spatial Audio, and smart lighting in my home to sync to the soundscape. 

While I'm disappointed this app isn't for me, it does seem really well made. They respect your privacy, and I especially love how you can preview their premium soundscapes before buying.

If you need some kind of sound mask to let you sleep, they have that covered too - set the time you want to be awakened and your lights will gently fade on over time (you can choose how gradually and use an audio alarm when it’s time to start your day if you need it.) Great UI, high quality sound and visuals, thoughtful design, many environments and regular updates. Come on, give it a try… whaddya have to lose? title: A Breath of Color in a Black-and-White World
content: Portal is an app that should be studied. It carefully and thoughtfully builds a captivating experience in the name of wellbeing. Upon running the app for the first time, being greeted with a stunning 8K-resolution environment was not only visually surprising, but was accompanied and held the hands of an auditory catharsis of 7.1 Dynamic Spatial Audio originating from the scene you’re placed in. In my home I have several smart lights, and you can imagine my surprise to see that by linking them to Portal, the colors instantly matched the setting, creating a depth of immersion. Instead of the push towards stress and pressure from other productivity apps, Portal encourages clarity and balance. From a circadian-based evolution of a day and night cycle, grants an environment that accompanies you throughout your day, or takes you to the rainforests of St. Lucia, or to Scottish castle walls on a breathtaking loch. All with the purpose of relaxation, sleep, or everyday focus. In an age of data harvesting and spying, Portal is transparent about their removal of analytics, data collection, and ad-trackers. And highlights the processes behind their making of a passion-project that doesn’t have to spell out that lthe team is in it for the long term. From the compassion and sincerity that the small independent team of friends and brothers, it suggests that focus grows gently, like nature itself. It reminded me that true productivity comes from steadiness, not rush. It’s rare to find an application, that feels both practical and nourishing, and this is the only app in which I was truly reminded that clarity, balance, and progress, are rooted in nature.

I quickly bought an annual subscription after trying this. Since then, I’ve used it almost everyday for many hours at a time. It is one of my favorite apps on the Mac. It helps block noise and keep me focused. 

That said, I recently canceled my renewal. In the past year and a half, there have only been two additional destinations: Costa Rica and the volcano. Neither one are interesting to me. The developers have repeatedly said much more is coming (nearly doubling portals according to one comment over a year ago), but nothing has come of it (look through the reviews). I wonder if they’ve lost interest. As of this review, the last update was many months ago and it was UI fixes. Their social media pages and blog have been quiet. I do wonder if this is still being developed.

I’ve also found that I really only use a handful of the portals over time. I’d use more, but so many of them feature birds, which is hard to listen to for long periods of time. If the birds could be turned off, it would be better. I also wish there were much more ocean/beach portals. 

I hate to give a critical review of an app I use so often. If the developers end up adding more destinations on a regular basis, I may resubscribe. Until then, I may just go back to YouTube.

If you try it and like it, it’s still probably worth an annual subscription. But, like me, I think you’ll find that the destinations need to be updated to justify annual renewals.

However, I bought the annual subscription last year for $49.99 from my I-Phone. And it says it’s $69.99 now from my IPad. I’m seeing two different prices from two different devices. I don’t really like that…So you could potentially be charged differently depending on the device you use. However, to be honest, I feel the number of available Portals is too limited relative to the subscription cost. While all the videos are premium quality, for a user like me who subscribes annually and habitually sets Portal as wallpaper immediately after startup every day, the current quantity and update frequency are indeed insufficient. This app is a game-changer, not just for individuals seeking a momentary escape or focus, but also for those like me, navigating the complexities of narcolepsy. It has also served as a wonderful tool in spending calming moments with my special needs child, enhancing our quality time together.

title: Great Curation and Backgrounds but needs a few more features
content:
I like many of the videos and audio the team has collected and curated. 

There are a several features that would make a really solid product even better.

First, if you have an 8k screen, this app has 8k screen backgrounds. It is currently one of the only ways and places to get some high quality 8k backgrounds. However, some like the iceland glacier icefield visibly shake/move a touch (probably needed a more stable tripod, but perhaps it was really windy there to get the shot). But kudos to the team for providing the high quality 8k content, it's truly next level if you have an 8k screen! Unfortunatly there is no easy way to find backgrounds by resolution, and I wish they would add that option to filter only for 8k etc.

Second, it would be great for there to be a 'dark mode' dynamic option where you could choose screens for early morning, morning, afternoon, late afternoon, early evening, and night time.  Maybe even have a 1st 2nd 3rd choice for each slot as well for it to auto cycle at some predetermined time (every hour or so).

Third, I have an 8k primary screen, but 3 other screens as well. It would be nice to be able to feed different backgrounds to the different screens (obviously only the audio from the primary screen would play--or maybe the audio of the last background desktop you click on, which can act as a way to let you know the last desktop you were working on).

Fourth, I see no way to make these backgrounds into screen savers, and I wish they would add that option too, and the ability to have the screen savers be different sets of backgrounds than your actual wallpaper backgrounds.

5th, the CPU usage goes between 500% to 1000% on my 2019 Mac Pro with 28 cores when showing 8k. It might be nice to have some lower CPU setting that maybe limits the frame rate, lowers the resolution, or just suspends the animation after some set amount of time so as not to eat up so many resources. An option to fade the audio out after some set period of time would also be nice. Also I notice it mostly hits the CPU and not much activity on the GPU so maybe offloading some of the processing load to the GPU would help.

Sixth and last, we need an abstract art set of backgrounds and space bacgrounds. Abstract a bit like the apple backgrounds maybe that animate. And space as in seeing maybe live constilations, or some nebula or something cool like that. I love nature, but having variety beyond nature would be great. I could see going from some natural landscapes for early moring to abstract art in the afternoon, to natural sun sets late afternoon, to some celstial shots for evening backgrounds.

I loathe subscriptions, and I applaud the developer adding a lifetime fee (albiet very high) and chose to buy the lifetime fee. 

Anyway, with adding those 6 features, the app would go from 4 to 5 stars for me.

title: A Gateway to Immersive Escapes: Portal App Review
content:
I recently discovered the macOS app Portal - Immersive Escapes, and I can confidently say that it has transformed my desktop experience in the most captivating way possible. This app has completely redefined the concept of desktop wallpapers, taking them from static images to breathtaking live views of awe-inspiring locations. It's an absolute gem!

First and foremost, the level of immersion that Portal provides is unparalleled. Every time I glance at my desktop, I'm instantly transported to a different place. Whether it's the serene beauty of a tropical beach, the majestic grandeur of a mountain range, or the vibrant energy of a bustling cityscape, I'm treated to a dynamic visual feast that never fails to captivate me.

What sets Portal apart is the attention to detail. The developers have not only provided stunning visuals but have also incorporated ambient sounds that match each location. The gentle waves crashing on the shore, the chirping of birds in a lush forest, or the distant sounds of a bustling market—it's the perfect symphony that complements the visual experience and makes it feel incredibly realistic.

The app itself is user-friendly and intuitive. It seamlessly integrates into macOS, allowing for easy customization and navigation. Setting up a new location as my wallpaper is as simple as a few clicks, and the app provides a vast collection of high-quality locations to choose from. Additionally, the option to schedule wallpaper changes based on the time of day or specific intervals adds an extra touch of variety to keep things fresh.

One aspect that pleasantly surprised me was the app's performance. Despite the dynamic nature of the live wallpapers, Portal has been incredibly efficient in terms of system resource usage. It runs smoothly in the background without affecting the overall performance of my Mac. This attention to optimization is commendable and greatly appreciated.

The developers behind Portal have consistently provided updates and new content, ensuring that the app remains fresh and exciting. They genuinely listen to user feedback and incorporate suggestions, making it clear that they are dedicated to delivering an exceptional experience to their users.

In conclusion, Portal - Immersive Escapes is a game-changer in the world of desktop customization. It goes above and beyond traditional wallpapers, transforming your workspace into a gateway to mesmerizing locations. With its stunning visuals, immersive sounds, user-friendly interface, and outstanding performance, this app has won my heart. I wholeheartedly recommend Portal to anyone seeking a truly captivating and immersive desktop experience.

Disclaimer: This review is based on my personal experience with the app and is in no way influenced or sponsored.

title: A subtle masterpiece of visual and audiable effects
content:
In my decades of wilderness travels, I've learned to appreciate the "pace" of scenic vistas -- in terms of their sounds, weather, and creature movements therein.  

Portal will make you feel "present" in beautifully curated scenic vistas while you work. 

Install Portal and select from among dozens of stunning scenic vistas for display on your desktop background.  Add headphones to "hear" them as well.  

Twenty minutes in, take a moment to clear your desktop and pause work for 5 minutes to look and listen carefully at Portal's scenic vista.   It is the moment when you discern a subtle "pace" -- of a spider's thread gently weaving itself in the breeze, a leaf falling, clouds slowly rising above glacial ice, sunlight movement through the mist etc -- THIS is what makes Portal's scenic vistas so magical and fresh through your day!

Portal artfully energizes my unconscious mind with subtle background visuals and audio effects while I work.   I am delighted to have found Portal!  With gratitude, my thanks goes to Stuart Chan and team!!

title: Shrill birds break my brain and other issues
content:
Almost loved it, but birds are loud, shrill and not relaxing. In all portals w birds, they are  not balanced w other frequencies for proportional, non-hearing loss atmosphere. This occurs when listening across different devices / settings, but worst in headphones. Like ice pick piercing thru center of my brain. Maybe include equaliser or mixer for user customisation?

Not much appealing ab starter package due to “immersive” = great for ppl w hearing loss, so I am just disappointed bc i REALLY love the concept, the aesthetic, features…

Oh yeah, except the alarm clock is half functional. That was the big feature i was looking forward to trying. The 24 hour clock option is a fail: setting alarm and display always show am/pm no matter my selection. Also, no way to sample the backup alarm choices: “singing bowls” or “morning (whatever its called)”…i know i will need it to wake me sooner or later, so i need to make sure it is a sound at a volume sufficient to do so. That’s just weird and seems like a bug (that it won’t play sample). So the features? They could be great, one day….

🫶the freebie to Ukraine 🇺🇦. Definitely get a star just for that. 

Basically, feels like work in progress though it looks exquisite in presentation / at first glance. Free version needs beefing up for those of us who are not rich and can’t scrape together $10/mo (or other pricing options) for what amounts to *better than average but not great* sound samples, pretty pictures, and some handy features that aren’t quite functional. The paid content library is mostly variations on the 3 typical themes: bodies of water sounds, precipitation sounds, and outdoor creatures (birds/crickets/frogs/etc). 

I will be honest and reiterate: I'm bitter bc i really wanted this app to work for me, and all the more bummed bc it doesn't. Frankly, I know that’s a tall order, so I am definitely rooting for improvements and success for the whole enterprise + it’s creators.

title: Favorite mindfulness app
content:
To the creators, thank you SO much for creating this app! I have loved using so many of its features, especially the alarms, timers, and breathing exercises. Oftentimes, I’ll keep a portal open all day when I’m at work to make the office a little more interesting and the spatial audio… amazing! It brings the portal that much more to life!

Really, I could go on about how much I love this app! And the response time to emailed questions is FAST (I had a “cat purring” suggestion and received a personalized message much quicker than I was expecting. It only made my experience with this company that much better). 

Alarms: The first favorite feature I’d like to highlight is the alarm. They’ve set it up in a way where you can choose a time to trigger the alarm, but you can also choose a time at which the alarm will  be at full volume (so you can enjoy a gradual birdsong which makes it feel like you’re actually waking up in nature, no matter the time of day). You’re also able to add a couple of chimes to go with the alarm if the sound is too soft or blends in too well. 
Timers: As you can probably tell from my previous favorite feature, I enjoy a gradual reminder rather than a sudden and/or blaring one. The timers are nice because you can enjoy the portal for however much time you’d like, and at the end it gradually fades to silence. 
Breathing Exercises: I’m a huge advocate for mindfulness breathing techniques to help with focusing, relaxing, etc. This feature is nicely implemented into the Focus tab of the app, and there is a gentle feedback rumble on the phone when the time has come to shift your phase (and they have a couple different techniques: 1:1, 4:4:4:4, etc.)
Updates: I feel like the Portal team does what they can to keep the updates up to speed with “the times”. I absolutely love the spatial audio feature (so much so that one time I was convinced it was actually raining, but it wasn’t!). 
All in all, this app is well worth the time, and if the availability is still the same, there is a free trial period where you can test it out. I’d say go for it!

title: Expensive But Gorgeous!
content:
In trying to find something to help me sleep peacefully, I’ve tried several apps. I wanted something soothing to play through the night. I tried a few relaxation apps and they were all fine with their white noise and raindrops, but nothing really captivated me. 

Then after seeing it come up so many times in my App Store searches, I tried Portal. Wow! Seriously WOW! These sounds are gorgeous! So rich, dimensional and lush! The visuals so cinematic! I would fire up a thunderstorm or windswept mountain peak and let my mind drift off. 

I liked the free offerings so much I tried the 7-day free trial and fell in love with several of the subscription soundscapes. But that price! As tempted as I was, I just couldn’t bring myself to spend that much right now. It was the $25 offer pop-up that convinced me to go for it. I’ve since started using the app to help me focus while reading, tried it with my headphones, and just tried one of the breathing exercises! It’s truly impressive! The developers have clearly put a lot of thought and effort into to making sure this isn’t just another cute collection of nature sounds. 

My only quibble is the price. To be fair, the developers acknowledge not everybody can afford this and don’t just brush off criticism with an “If you don’t want to pay, go somewhere else” attitude. Definitely a plus in my book. 

I’d love to see a smart TV app in the future, as the immersive sound and stunning visuals would be perfect for the medium. 

Whether you can afford a subscription or not, I highly encourage anyone looking for a relaxation app to give this one a shot. It’s one of the best!

title: Amazing UI and Phenomenal Customer Service
content: I was initially resistant to try Portal because of concerns about getting to interested in an app with a high subscription cost. However, the nice permanent free offering convinced me that some things are worth it. This app is extraordinary. First, it respects your privacy and collects no data on you which is a rarity these days. Then, if you love soundscapes you will not find a better program to transport you around the world. The sound quality is excellent and the time between loops is long enough to be near imperceptible. The UI makes exploring interesting and seamless. Integration with the 3D audio is great too though I usually do have my phone use speaker or Bluetooth. My only gripe is if my phone is not plugged in overnight, the background battery usage can be more than I expect (10-15%) on an IPhone 13 Pro, as the battery usage chart shows it is active overnight. This may be nothing though. I had questions and a problem with purchasing the app and the team could not have been more helpful. I hope one day the permanent purchase price is more affordable. I look forward to further integrating this app into my workflows. Keep up the great work team! Always excited for new portals!
